errors.where: js/data-questions.js, QUESTIONS c-c9ijyeac, stem: "Teramo's hills in the north of Abruzzo carry the region's own DOCG for Montepulciano." and explanation: "the tiny Tullum zone at Tollo, promoted in 2019, also holds DOCG rank."
errors.claim: Abruzzo has one Montepulciano DOCG (Colline Teramane), with Tullum as the only other DOCG.
errors.correction: Abruzzo now has three DOCGs: Montepulciano d'Abruzzo Colline Teramane (2003), Tullum or Terre Tollesi (2019) and Casauria (registered in 2025, formerly a sub-zone of Montepulciano d'Abruzzo, at least 90 per cent Montepulciano). The key stands; the explanation should name Casauria, as the abruzzo article already does.
errors.source: Gazzetta Ufficiale, registration of Casauria as a DOP with the traditional term DOCG, 22 November 2025 (cited in the abruzzo article's sources); gamberorosso.it, Casauria in Abruzzo, una nuova DOCG, 2025.

courtUpdates.now: Montepulciano d'Abruzzo has a third DOCG beside Colline Teramane and Tullum: Casauria, in the province of Pescara, a former sub-zone of the DOC raised in 2025 and requiring at least 90 per cent Montepulciano. The regional DOC also writes provincial sub-zones onto its Superiore and Riserva labels from the 2023 harvest (decree of 19 January 2023).
courtUpdates.source: Gazzetta Ufficiale, 22 November 2025 (Casauria DOP and DOCG); gamberorosso.it and gamberorossointernational.com, Casauria a new DOCG in Abruzzo; Consorzio Tutela Vini d'Abruzzo, the 2023 sub-zone reform (vinidabruzzo.it).

This is the Court's shortest Italian table and the Codex covers every row with stems in both banks except the producers; the one service cell (decant young Taurasi and Sagrantino) rests on the general decanting stems and the table's young tannic row, which names Barolo but neither Taurasi nor Sagrantino. Court cells to read with care: the Court's Location sentence repeats the Tuscany page word for word (Ligurian Sea to the Apennines), which fits Tuscany and not the south; and the heading Match DOCG to Major Region sits over two Verdicchio wines it prints as DOC, which they are, while their Riserva versions are DOCG (the abruzzo article's Marche note says so). Two searches allowed; one spent, on Casauria. No other change to the Court's cells since 8.2023 was found: Taurasi, Fiano di Avellino and Greco di Tufo (DOCG 1993 and 2003) and Montefalco Sagrantino (1992) stand as printed.
